sources.name: Land contamination risk management
sources.fact: Environment Agency LCRM sets the staged risk-based process for assessing and managing historic land contamination

sources.name: LCRM before you start
sources.fact: LCRM requires competent assessment and can cover planning, liabilities, remediation and regulatory contexts

sources.name: Planning land affected by contamination
sources.fact: Planning requires source-pathway-receptor assessment and may require desk study, walkover, investigation and remediation evidence

sources.name: EA voluntary remediation advice
sources.fact: June 2026 service provides site-specific regulatory advice where contamination affects controlled waters outside specified planning consultation contexts

sources.name: Waste environmental permits
sources.fact: Waste treatment/storage/disposal may require environmental permits; permit status is activity-specific

sources.name: Apply for an environmental permit
sources.fact: 2026 online permit service includes mobile plant land remediation and waste treatment activities

sources.name: Waste recovery plans
sources.fact: May 2026 guidance requires evidence and risk assessment for deposit-for-recovery activities

sources.name: Land remediation deployment guidance
sources.fact: 2026 deployment guidance requires appropriate mobile plant permit or bespoke permitting where conditions are not met

sources.name: Contaminated soil RPS 215
sources.fact: RPS 215 is conditional regulatory enforcement position and does not remove underlying permit requirements generally

sources.name: Surface water and groundwater discharge permits
sources.fact: Discharges of polluting wastewater to surface water or ground may require environmental permits

sources.name: LBBD land contamination
sources.fact: LBBD identifies contamination from historic/commercial/industrial activity as potentially affecting people, buildings, water and nature

sources.name: Check environmental permit requirement
sources.fact: Activities that may pollute land/water, increase flood risk or affect drainage may require permits or licences

examples: Historic industrial use is a screening signal, not proof that a parcel is contaminated
A contaminated-land register or council enquiry does not quantify remediation cost
Desk study and walkover are preliminary evidence and may lead to intrusive investigation
Permit requirement depends on the remediation/waste activity and cannot be inferred from planning status alone
RPS 215 is conditional and does not equal a general exemption
Controlled-water contamination needs site-specific source-pathway-receptor evidence
Successful remediation requires verification; planned remediation is not completed remediation
No land-value or buildability uplift is assigned without site investigation, remediation design and verification evidence
